title: Sequential hypothesis enforcer for safe A/B model upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an opinionated A/B experiment controller that enforces sequential hypothesis testing, pre-registered metrics, and automated rollback rules for model version upgrades. The controller should support: (1) staged exposure (microsplits -> canary -> ramp), (2) shadow probing with sample-synchronous mirroring, (3) multimetric verdicts (primary metric + guardrail metrics), (4) dynamic alpha spending to preserve statistical validity across multiple looks, and (5) automated rollback/failfast triggers with a human-in-the-loop notification flow. Primary customers: platform teams and ML engineers deploying model upgrades across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can define experiments with pre-registered primary and guardrail metrics and expected directionality
Support for staged exposure schedule: 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% with configurable step durations
Sequential testing logic implemented (alpha spending via O'Brien-Fleming or Pocock-like schedules) to maintain overall false positive control
Shadow probing mode available to mirror 100% of traffic without affecting live routing and record paired outputs for offline drift comparisons
Automated rollback policy: immediate rollback when primary metric regression exceeds configured threshold AND at least one guardrail is violated, with an option for auto-wean-back vs full revert
Console UI surfaces per-step statistical reports, cumulative alpha used, sample sizes, and decision rationale; APIs expose same data programmatically
End-to-end telemetry and audit logs (which model variant saw which request, paired shadow outputs, decision timestamps) are stored for 90 days by default
Integration test that simulates synthetic traffic with injected regressions and verifies the controller halts rollout and triggers notifications
notes: Trade-offs discussed: we prefer sequential testing to frequentist repeated t-tests because teams run many partial looks; however, sequential methods add complexity to UI and education
We will initially support two alpha spend schedules (conservative and permissive) and expose custom alpha curves later
Shadow probing will only mirror non-sensitive request metadata by default; engineering will add PII filters per customer requirements
This feature surfaces in Console under 'Model experiments' and in the API under /experiments/v1; backend controller will live in the rollout service
